Hi Satoshi — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the confusion. We sometimes see Calendly incorrectly infer zones when a browser or OS prefers UTC offsets during DST transitions.

Couple quick options:
- If you prefer Calendly, try selecting the timezone dropdown at the top of the scheduling page and set it to (GMT+9) Tokyo. That usually fixes it.
- If that still looks off, I can send a manual ICS invite pinned to 10:00 JST and invite both you and Liam.

I’m looping in Marissa (our APAC SE) to advise on the ICS and to confirm availability.

Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/kickoff-demo

Hey Kim —

We've had this exact behavior with a handful of APAC customers around DST cutover weeks. Short checklist I use:
1) Ask them to confirm the time they want in their local TZ (you already have 10:00 JST).
2) Create a manual calendar event in your Google calendar using the event timezone = Asia/Tokyo, set for 10:00 local, then export as .ics. That pins the event to Japan time regardless of how Calendly renders.
3) Send the .ics and a plain-text invite with the UTC and local time (e.g., 10:00 JST / 01:00 UTC) so everyone is clear.

I can create the ICS if you like and drop it to you to send — Viv, can you confirm Kim's availability windows listed in HubSpot? (I think 10/14–10/16 mornings PT was noted).

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for being flexible. I created a manual invite pinned to Asia/Tokyo for:

- Time: 10:00–10:30 JST (01:00–01:30 UTC)
